items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: Worked with Sig Meyer and some hands off. It was a good band.

ctx.x: Well, my mother speaks seven different languages and I don't speak one good one. I didn't stay home. I tell you, I was a rat man. And I'm the oldest one that needed all of the language. My brother and sister got them and they stayed home. And I didn't all try to use them, you know what I mean? You were the only smart one. Yeah. I'd go home sometimes, I'd be home about every day before I could understand things. Mama was trying to ask me questions. Why does he drive some coffee to the team, son?

Yeah, I wouldn't mind a little cup of coffee. If you have an extra cup then. Sure. What do you want in it? Just a little sugar and cream. See, we had one of the first swing bands in Chicago, you know. Worked with Sig Meyer and some hands off. It was a good band. How big was the band? How much sugar do you want? One and a half, right? One, two, three, five, seven, ten pieces. Sig Meyer, he played the violin, he was the leader. It was a very good band. Was it a reading band arrangements and so on? Oh yes. You know…
Who? Wrath. You know the guitar player? Oh, I didn't know that. Yeah, because he used to play with George. He used to play with a big, heavy-shaped guy. Oh, I didn't know that. He played a long bass.

items.title: Muggsy Spanier Interview, 1961-02-02
items.q: I worked with Arnold Lloyd Cannon with Sig Meyer. We had a band.

ctx.x: I worked with Arnold Lloyd Cannon with Sig Meyer. We had a band. Oh, yeah. You had a picture of that band. Yeah. It was one of the few swing bands in that area in Chicago. We had a good band, too. Volley Defoe was in that band, too.
How did Volley sound in the old days? Wonderful. I know he played a little bit with the Friars Inn group.
